newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index posts second biggest gain ever.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index posts second biggest gain ever.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average soared to its second biggest point gain ever Thursday, spurred by a powerful bond market rally and a flurry of options-related buying.

The 30-stock Dow ended up 126.87 points, or 2 percent, at 6,473.64, its biggest rise since the blue-chip index soared 184.86 on Oct. 21, 1987. The powerful rally saw 26 of the 30 Dow components close higher.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,806 to 753 on heavy volume of 522 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"This may be the start of the Santa Claus rally," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
For two straight sessions this week, stocks had managed to move higher despite an uncooperative bond market.

But Thursday's economic reports, including a downbeat report from the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's business conditions survey for its region and a surprising rise in new jobless claims, sparked a big jump in long-term bonds and a drop in interest rates.
"The big surprise today was the decline in the Philly Fed survey," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.
"That was important because it was our first look at December numbers and it told us the economy was slower than in November," he said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond jumped 1-1/2 points, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.59 percent from 6.70 percent at Wednesday's close.
The Philadelphia Fed reported a drop in its business conditions index, suggesting a potential December slowdown.

The index declined 2.2 after rising 6.4 in November as new orders, shipments, backlogs and hiring deteriorated. Looking ahead six months, though, survey respondents were optimistic about a pickup in orders.

Analysts cautioned against reading too much into the stock's performance, noting that Friday's triple-witching expiration of futures, options, and index options likely exaggerated the market's action.

While the rally was impressive, it fell short of the Dow's scorching 186.84-point run on Oct. 21, 1987, a climb that took the index up more than 10 percent to 2,027.85. That gain came two days after the Dow crashed 508.0 points to 1,738.74 in its biggest one-day drop.
On a percentage basis, however, Thursday's gains were not even in the top 10.
Widespread buying interest helped stocks overcome a profit warning from General Motors Corp., which had threatened to cast a pall over the entire market.

Several Wall Street brokerage houses slashed their fourth quarter earnings estimates on GM after the carmaker told analysts late Wednesday that its results would be hurt by high costs associated with marketing a host of new models.
"In the old days, what was bad for GM was bad for the country," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "That certainly does not seem to be the case today."

Among other issues, General Electric Co. jumped 3-1/2 to 102-3/4 after announcing a two-for-one stock split, a 13 percent jump in its quarterly dividend and a $4 billion increase in its share repurchase programme.
Nike Inc. climbed 1-7/8 to 60-3/4, extending Wednesday's gain on the company's strong quarterly earnings. Fila Holdings SpA joined in the rally, rising 4-7/8 to 64-3/4.

Micro Warehouse Inc. slid 7-1/2 to 12-1/2 after saying that its fourth quarter earnings would be well below analysts' estimates. It blamed the disappointing results on strong competition in its sales of Macintosh computer and higher operating costs.
Another Macintosh retailer, Multiple Zones International Inc. also said its fourth quarter earnings would be depressed. Multiple Zones tumbled 7-3/4 to 10-1/2.
Apple Computer Inc., which makes the Macintosh computer line, fell 7/8 to 22-1/4.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 10.48 points to 1,295.86
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 14.22 to 745.76. The American Stock Exchange index gained 3.57 to 578.53.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 6.99 to 392.16. The average share rose 73 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,202.495 up 119.25 or 1.68 percent.
